full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN-VARIANT, with low-to-medium confidence.** The hyperuniform r⁻⁴ correlations are a well-documented class. I found no source for this exact L-shaped, left-turning lattice rule, and none for the turning-optimum and square-root-cusp features.

**1. Model family.** This is a stochastic conserved-mass transport (mass-redistribution) lattice model that breaks time-reversal and parity (chiral). The relevant literature is nonequilibrium statistical physics, specifically hyperuniformity from conservation laws. Two ingredients matter:
- Conserved noise with center-of-mass (dipole) conservation gives a structure factor S(q) ~ q².
- In d=2, S(q) ~ q² corresponds to density correlations decaying as r^-(d+2) = r⁻⁴. This is my own inference, not something I read in the sources.

**2. What the literature shows**
- **Hexner & Levine 2015, PRL 114, 110602, "Hyperuniformity of critical absorbing states."** Conserved directed percolation absorbing states are hyperuniform at the critical point, with anomalously small density fluctuations. This is the early origin of the center-of-mass-conservation route to hyperuniformity.
- **Lei, Ciamarra & Ni 2019, Sci. Adv., "Nonequilibrium strongly hyperuniform fluids of circle active particles."** This is the chiral-active case. Fickian diffusion at large scales and local center-of-mass-conserving noise are responsible for the global hyperuniformity. It reports S(q→0) ~ q². I checked the title and venue against the search result. I did not confirm the author list or year from the page, so those come from memory.
- **Kuroda & Miyazaki 2023, J. Stat. Mech., "Microscopic theory for hyperuniformity in two-dimensional chiral active fluid."** They derive a fluctuating hydrodynamic equation whose linear analysis captures hyperuniformity. They also argue it has the same form as the macroscopic description of the random organization model with center-of-mass conservation. This ties chirality to center-of-mass-conserving hydrodynamics.
- **Hazra, Mukherjee & Pradhan 2025, J. Stat. Mech., "Hyperuniformity in mass transport processes with center-of-mass conservation: some exact results."** This is the closest lattice mass-transport analogue and the best review-like source I found. In d=1 and 2 it finds S(q) ~ q², implying class-I spatial hyperuniformity.
- **Mukherjee, Tapader, Hazra & Pradhan 2024, PRE 110, 024119.** This covers center-of-mass-conserving systems with broken time-reversal symmetry. Center-of-mass conservation makes the mobility vanish exactly.
- **Maire et al. 2025, J. Chem. Phys. 163, 214507, "Hyperuniformity and conservation laws in non-equilibrium systems."** It gives a general mechanism and S(k) ~ k^m, with m set by the number of conserved multipole moments. It also finds that hyperuniformity from conserved noise plus partially conserved average motion is not robust against non-linear perturbations. I saw only the abstract, so I can't say whether it contains a model like this one.

**3. What differs, and whether it likely matters**
- The L-shaped, always-left two-hop rule with a 40%/60% split and a tunable turning strength is not a rule I found in any of these papers. The chiral hyperuniformity papers use off-lattice particles (circle swimmers, spinners). The lattice papers use center-of-mass-conserving rules without a chiral turn.
- The r⁻⁴ decay and the isotropy (xy ratio 1) match the generic q² class, so I expect them to be known.
- The turning-strength optima that minimise long-wavelength fluctuations, and the square-root cusp near maximal turning, were not found in any source I read. They may simply be how the q² coefficient depends on the parameters, but I could not confirm that.
- The closed-box edge current is the generic chiral edge-current phenomenon, which is well known (for example in active chiral matter).

**5. Confidence: low to medium.** The class identification is well supported, but I could not read the full texts of Hazra et al. or Maire et al. A model like this one may be there. The search tool gave only abstracts and snippets, so the quantitative turning-optimum and cusp claims are unverified either way. I did not reach "LITERATURE-SILENT" because the underlying phenomenon is clearly described.
